glosses: A physician; a member of the medical profession; one who is trained and licensed to heal the sick or injured. The final examination and qualification may award a doctor degree in which case the post-nominal letters are DO, DPM, MD, DMD, or DDS in the US, or MBBS or BDS in the UK.

examples.text: If you still feel unwell tomorrow, see your doctor.
By medicine life may be prolonged, yet death / Will seize the doctor too.

glosses: A person who has attained a doctorate, such as a Ph.D. or Th.D. or one of many other terminal degrees conferred by a college or university.
A veterinarian; a medical practitioner who treats non-human animals.
A nickname for a person who has special knowledge or talents to manipulate or arrange transactions.
A teacher; one skilled in a profession or a branch of knowledge; a learned man.

examples.text: So from that tyme forwarde I began to ſmell the word of god, and forſoke the ſchole doctors and ſuch foolries.
one of the doctors of Italy, Nicholas Macciavel

glosses: Any mechanical contrivance intended to remedy a difficulty or serve some purpose in an exigency.

examples.text: the doctor of a calico-printing machine, which is a knife to remove superfluous colouring matter
the doctor, or auxiliary engine, also called "donkey engine"
The use of a disk doctor may be the only way of recovering valuable data following a disk crash.

glosses: A fish, the friar skate.
A ship's cook.

examples.text: His galley is small, and, microscopic as it is, it is shared by his brother in misery, the ship's cook, he whom the crew familiarly know as the “Doctor.”
[…] old Scotch Jem the boatswain, tunes his fiddle, and the doctor, (ship's cook,) produces his tambourine; the men dance on deck, […]

glosses: To act as a medical doctor to.

examples.text: Her children doctored her back to health.

glosses: To act as a medical doctor.

examples.text:
2017, "Do No Harm", season 8, episode 2 of Adventure Time
Doctor Princess: Put this on. [gives her lab coat to Finn] OK, you're a doctor now. Good luck.
Finn: Wait, wait, whoa, whoa, whoa, wait! I don't know how to doctor!

glosses: To make (someone) into an (academic) doctor; to confer a doctorate upon.
To physically alter (medically or surgically) a living being in order to change growth or behavior.

examples.text: They doctored their apple trees by vigorous pruning, and now the dwarfed trees are easier to pick.
We may legally doctor a pet to reduce its libido.

glosses: To genetically alter an extant species.

examples.text: Mendel's discoveries showed how the evolution of a species may be doctored.

glosses: To alter or make obscure, as with the intention to deceive, especially a document.

examples.text: To doctor the signature of an instrument with intent to defraud is an example of forgery.

That picture – the one that Andrew claimed on BBC’s Newsnight might have been doctored, since he had “no recollection” of then or ever meeting Giuffre at Tramp nightclub in London – will likely serve as both a prequel and postscript of the saga.

Catherine, the Princess of Wales, apologized on Monday for doctoring a photo of her with her three children, which was recalled by several news agencies on Sunday after they determined the image had been manipulated.

glosses: To adulterate, drug, or poison (drink).
To take medicine.

glosses: De médecin, des médecins.

examples.text: le doigt medecin ou le doigt annulaire

Digito medico. Le doigt médecin est le quatrième doigt. Il n’y a pas la moindre raison à cette dénomination bizarre ; car jamais médecin n’emploie le quatrième doigt ni plus fréquemment que les autres, ni à quelque usage particulier ; […]

glosses: Personne qui a un diplôme de docteur en médecine. Professionnel de santé chargé de guérir et soigner les maladies, les pathologies, les blessures.

examples.text: D’ailleurs la médecine, surtout comme la plupart des médecins la pratiquent aujourd’hui, n’est qu’une espèce de flatterie; et, à cet égard, on peut dire qu’elle ne ressemble pas mal à la rhétorique.
Halpersohn, qui passa, pendant cinq ou six ans, pour un médicastre, à cause de ses poudres, de ses médecines, possédait la science innée des grands médecins.

En 1495, on cite une vieille médecienne. Il faut faire appeler la « vieille médecienne et lui demander, en présence des médecins, ce qu’elle a donné à la femme » (malade). Nous voyons donc que les femmes-médecins étaient répandues en Allemagne.
Privé de ce casuel, il ne nous serait plus possible d’indemniser notre médecin. Conséquence: plus de soins gratuits aux indigents.
Mais on dérape très vite, le médecin est aussi fou que ses patients, les infirmières sont déchaînées, l’atmosphère vire au pandémonium morbide et sexué.

Si la médecin était toujours restée en Bretagne, Léanne avait d’abord déménagé avec ses parents, quand son père avait été muté au centre de transmission de la Marine nationale à Rosnay, dans le Berry.
La première famille est celle d’Ariane Benoit, médecin québécoise, mère monoparentale déjà fortement éprouvée par les méfaits de son premier mari.
Sans médecin, je me soigne chez le pharmacien

glosses: Dans l’armée française, premier grade militaire conféré aux médecins diplômés officiers du Corps de Santé des Armées, à l’issue de leur internat.
Remède ; ce qui soigne.

examples.text:
C’est le chabrol qui ravigote,
Il est le plus grand des médecins,
Il vous réchauffe le gosier
Et brise le mal en morceaux.

glosses: Guérisseur.

examples.text: En certains cas, le médecin de l’âme est plus nécessaire que le médecin du corps.
Le temps est un grand médecin.
